mission.title: thanos: [Feature] Per-Store TLS configuration in Thanos Query
mission.description: Feature request for Thanos Query to talk to some StoreAPI endpoints over plain gRPC while using different TLS settings for other endpoints. The original issue came from operators running an in-cluster store without TLS and remote stores in other clusters with TLS enabled. The practical solution is to switch Query from one global gRPC client TLS configuration to file-based endpoint discovery with default_client_config and per-endpoint client_config overrides.

steps.title: Inspect how Query currently connects to StoreAPI endpoints
steps.description:
Start by checking whether your Query deployment still uses global gRPC client flags such as `--grpc-client-tls-*` together with static `--endpoint` or `--store` arguments. Those global flags apply to every remote store equally and are the reason mixed TLS and non-TLS topologies are hard to express.

```bash
kubectl -n monitoring get deploy thanos-query -o yaml | sed -n '/containers:/,/volumes:/p'
kubectl -n monitoring get configmap thanos-query-endpoints -o yaml 2>/dev/null || echo "No endpoint SD ConfigMap yet"
kubectl -n monitoring get secret | grep thanos-query
```
Look for a topology like this: one in-cluster sidecar/store reachable as plain gRPC traffic and one or more cross-cluster stores that require a CA bundle, SNI/server name, or mTLS client certificate.

steps.title: Create an endpoint SD file with default and per-endpoint TLS settings
steps.description:
Model the Query connections in a YAML file instead of repeating CLI flags. Put shared defaults in `default_client_config`, then override only the remote stores that need stronger TLS settings. This is the key technical change behind the feature request: Query can keep talking insecurely to local stores while using a distinct TLS client config for each remote store.

```yaml
default_client_config:
  tls_config:
    enabled: false
  compression: snappy

endpoints:
  - address: thanos-sidecar.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:10901

  - address: thanos-store.eu1.example.com:10901
    client_config:
      tls_config:
        enabled: true
        ca_file: /etc/thanos/certs/eu1/ca.crt
      server_name: thanos-store.eu1.example.com

  - address: thanos-store.us1.example.com:10901
    client_config:
      tls_config:
        enabled: true
        cert_file: /etc/thanos/certs/us1/client.crt
        key_file: /etc/thanos/certs/us1/client.key
        ca_file: /etc/thanos/certs/us1/ca.crt
      server_name: thanos-store.us1.example.com
```
Important details:
- `client_config` overrides `default_client_config` for just one endpoint.
- Omitting a field inherits the default; setting a field to an empty string explicitly clears an inherited value.
- TLS is only overridable for file-based endpoint discovery, not for endpoints supplied solely by static CLI flags or DNS SD.

steps.title: Mount the endpoint file and certificates into the Query pod
steps.description:
Store the endpoint discovery YAML in a ConfigMap, store remote CA/client certs in a Secret, and update the Query deployment to read them. This turns the feature request into an actionable rollout plan.

```bash
kubectl -n monitoring create configmap thanos-query-endpoints \
  --from-file=endpoints.yaml=./endpoints.yaml \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

kubectl -n monitoring create secret generic thanos-query-store-certs \
  --from-file=eu1/ca.crt=./eu1-ca.crt \
  --from-file=us1/ca.crt=./us1-ca.crt \
  --from-file=us1/client.crt=./us1-client.crt \
  --from-file=us1/client.key=./us1-client.key \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```
Example deployment fragment:

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: thanos-query
          args:
            - query
            - --http-address=0.0.0.0:10902
            - --grpc-address=0.0.0.0:10901
            - --endpoint.sd-config-file=/etc/thanos/endpoints/endpoints.yaml
          volumeMounts:
            - name: endpoint-sd
              mountPath: /etc/thanos/endpoints
              readOnly: true
            - name: store-certs
              mountPath: /etc/thanos/certs
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: endpoint-sd
          configMap:
            name: thanos-query-endpoints
        - name: store-certs
          secret:
            secretName: thanos-query-store-certs
```
If you still have deprecated global flags like `--grpc-client-tls-secure` or `--grpc-client-tls-ca`, remove them after migrating so they do not mask endpoint-specific behavior.

steps.title: Verify mixed secure and insecure stores are healthy
steps.description:
After rollout, confirm that Query discovers every store and that TLS failures are limited to the endpoint that is misconfigured.

```bash
kubectl -n monitoring rollout status deploy/thanos-query
kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/thanos-query --since=10m | egrep "endpoint|store|tls|grpc"
kubectl -n monitoring port-forward deploy/thanos-query 10902:10902
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:10902/api/v1/stores | jq '.data[] | {name: .name, lastError: .lastError}'
```
Healthy output should show the local in-cluster store connected without TLS and the remote stores connected with their own CA/server-name/client-certificate settings. If one remote endpoint fails hostname verification or mTLS authentication, only that store should report `lastError`, which makes debugging much easier than a single global TLS toggle.

resolution.summary: Thanos Query solved this class of deployments by allowing per-endpoint client configuration in file-based service discovery. Instead of forcing one global `--grpc-client-tls-*` setting onto every StoreAPI connection, operators can define shared defaults and then override TLS, CA bundles, SNI, client certificates, and compression for specific remote stores. This is especially useful when one Query instance fans out to a mix of in-cluster non-TLS sidecars and cross-cluster TLS-protected stores.
codeSnippets:
default_client_config:
  tls_config:
    enabled: false

endpoints:
  - address: thanos-sidecar.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:10901

  - address: thanos-store.remote.example.com:10901
    client_config:
      tls_config:
        enabled: true
        ca_file: /etc/thanos/certs/remote/ca.crt
        cert_file: /etc/thanos/certs/remote/client.crt
        key_file: /etc/thanos/certs/remote/client.key
      server_name: thanos-store.remote.example.com

args:
  - query
  - --endpoint.sd-config-file=/etc/thanos/endpoints/endpoints.yaml
volumeMounts:
  - name: endpoint-sd
    mountPath: /etc/thanos/endpoints
    readOnly: true
  - name: store-certs
    mountPath: /etc/thanos/certs
    readOnly: true

kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/thanos-query --since=10m | egrep "endpoint|store|tls|grpc"
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:10902/api/v1/stores | jq '.data[] | {name: .name, lastError: .lastError}'

prerequisites.description: Access to a Kubernetes cluster running Thanos Query plus at least one StoreAPI endpoint. You should be able to edit the Query Deployment, create ConfigMaps and Secrets for endpoint discovery and certificates, and inspect Query logs or the /api/v1/stores endpoint.
